newsitem.title: USA: Occidental profits up more than expected in quarter.
newsitem.headline: Occidental profits up more than expected in quarter.

text.p: Occidental Petroleum Corp. said Thursday its profits rose sharply in the first quarter, boosted by higher oil and gas prices and growth in the company's core businesses.

Net income rose to $179 million, or 47 cents per share, in the quarter ended March 31 from $134 million, or 35 cents per share, in the year-ago period. The 1996 first-quarter results included a one-time after-tax loss of $30 million from the early retirement of high-coupon debt.
Earnings per share before one-time items rose to 47 cents from 44 cents, exceeding analysts' consensus estimate of 43 cents.
Sales grew to $2.8 billion from $2.5 billion.

"Our improved earnings in the first quarter of 1997 reflect higher oil and gas prices," said Ray Irani, chairman and chief executive. "We continue our strategy to increase earnings by growing our core businesses while reducing debt and operating costs."

Oil and gas division earnings rose to $228 million from $161 million for the 1996 first quarter, mainly due to higher worldwide crude oil and natural gas prices and cost benefits from a reorganization. This was partially offset by higher taxes, depreciation and exploration expense, it said.
Natural gas transmission division earnings fell to $91 million from $121 million, due mainly to lower margins on sales and transportation.
Chemical division earnings also slid to $92 million from $118 million as a result of higher feedstock and raw material costs and an outage at Occidental's Bayport, Texas, facility.
Interest expense dropped to $101 million from $130 million as Occidental lowered its average debt levels by retiring debt early in 1996 and as interest rates fell, the company said.
